examples: Summers in that coastal city are hot and humid, making the air feel heavy.
تابستان‌ها در آن شهر ساحلی گرم و مرطوب است و هوا سنگین به نظر می‌رسد.
The greenhouse stays humid year-round to help the tropical plants thrive.
گلخانه در تمام سال مرطوب می‌ماند تا به رشد گیاهان گرمسیری کمک کند.
She found the humid climate hard to adjust to after years in the desert.
او بعد از سال‌ها زندگی در بیابان، سازگاری با آب‌وهوای مرطوب را دشوار یافت.
miniContext: Humid describes air that contains a high level of moisture, often making the weather feel sticky or uncomfortably warm even when the temperature itself is not extreme. Tropical regions tend to be humid year-round, and a bathroom becomes humid after a hot shower. The word is frequently paired with 'hot' because high humidity makes heat feel more intense.

examples: The magician made the coin vanish right in front of the audience's eyes.
شعبده‌باز سکه را درست جلوی چشم تماشاگران ناپدید کرد.
Her fear seemed to vanish the moment she stepped onto the stage.
ترس او به نظر می‌رسید همان لحظه که روی صحنه رفت ناپدید شده باشد.
The hiking trail seemed to vanish into the thick fog ahead of them.
مسیر کوهنوردی به نظر می‌رسید در مه غلیظ پیش رویشان ناپدید می‌شود.
miniContext: To vanish means to disappear suddenly and completely, often in a way that feels surprising or mysterious. Morning mist can vanish once the sun rises, and a person's savings can vanish quickly after a bad investment. The word suggests a swift, almost magical disappearance rather than a slow fading away.

examples: The hikers got lost in the dense forest after sunset.
کوهنوردان بعد از غروب آفتاب در جنگل انبوه راهشان را گم کردند.
Dense fog along the highway forced drivers to slow down considerably.
مه متراکم در امتداد بزرگراه رانندگان را مجبور کرد به‌طور قابل‌توجهی سرعتشان را کم کنند.
The textbook was so dense with information that students had to read each page twice.
کتاب درسی آن‌قدر پر از اطلاعات بود که دانش‌آموزان باید هر صفحه را دو بار می‌خواندند.
miniContext: Dense describes something tightly packed, whether it is a forest with trees close together, fog thick enough to block visibility, or writing so packed with ideas that it is hard to follow quickly. A densely populated city has many people living in a small area, and a dense material, like lead, is heavy relative to its size. The word always points to a high concentration of something within a given space.

examples: Meteorologists predict heavy rain for the weekend across the region.
هواشناسان بارش شدید را برای آخر هفته در سراسر منطقه پیش‌بینی می‌کنند.
No one could predict how the young player would perform under so much pressure.
هیچ‌کس نمی‌توانست پیش‌بینی کند آن بازیکن جوان تحت این‌همه فشار چگونه عمل خواهد کرد.
Analysts predict a sharp rise in housing prices next year.
تحلیلگران افزایش شدید قیمت مسکن را برای سال آینده پیش‌بینی می‌کنند.
miniContext: To predict something means to say in advance what you believe will happen, usually based on evidence, experience, or careful reasoning. Weather forecasters predict storms using satellite data, economists predict market trends using historical patterns, and a wise friend might predict how a conversation will go based on past behavior. A prediction can turn out right or wrong, but it is always a statement made before the event occurs.

examples: In the movie, the villain plots to take over the entire city.
در فیلم، شخص شرور قصد دارد کنترل کل شهر را به دست بگیرد.
The novel's villain is far more interesting than its rather dull hero.
شخص شرور رمان بسیار جالب‌تر از قهرمان نسبتاً کسل‌کننده‌اش است.
Fans were surprised when the once-trusted character turned out to be the villain all along.
طرفداران شگفت‌زده شدند وقتی شخصیتی که زمانی قابل‌اعتماد بود، معلوم شد از ابتدا شخص شرور بوده است.
miniContext: A villain is a character, usually in a story, film, or play, who behaves wickedly and often opposes the hero. Classic villains plot evil schemes, betray their allies, or seek power at any cost, giving the story its central conflict. The word can also be used loosely outside fiction to describe someone widely blamed for causing harm, as in 'the villain of the financial crisis.'

examples: Vapor rose from the hot cup of tea on the cold morning.
در آن صبح سرد، بخار از فنجان داغ چای بلند می‌شد.
The engineer explained how water vapor condenses into clouds at high altitude.
مهندس توضیح داد چگونه بخار آب در ارتفاع بالا به ابر تبدیل می‌شود.
A thin layer of vapor covered the bathroom mirror after her shower.
لایه‌ای نازک از بخار بعد از دوش گرفتن او، آینه حمام را پوشانده بود.
miniContext: Vapor is the gaseous form of a substance that is normally liquid or solid, most commonly associated with water vapor rising from something hot or evaporating in the air. Steam from a kettle, mist over a lake at dawn, and the fog on a cold window are all forms of vapor. Scientists study how vapor behaves as it cools and condenses back into liquid droplets.

examples: The whale they spotted from the boat was absolutely enormous.
نهنگی که از قایق مشاهده کردند واقعاً بسیار بزرگ بود.
Winning the lottery would make an enormous difference to her family's life.
بردن در بخت‌آزمایی تفاوت عظیمی در زندگی خانواده او ایجاد می‌کرد.
The company suffered an enormous loss after the factory fire.
شرکت بعد از آتش‌سوزی کارخانه، ضرر عظیمی را متحمل شد.
miniContext: Enormous describes something far larger than usual in size, scale, or degree, often large enough to seem surprising or overwhelming. An enormous crowd gathered for the concert, and scientists sometimes discover an enormous gap between two measurements that challenges their assumptions. The word works for physical size as well as abstract things like pressure, pride, or disappointment.

examples: Scientists developed a new theory to explain how the universe began.
دانشمندان نظریه جدیدی برای توضیح چگونگی آغاز جهان ارائه دادند.
Detectives had a theory about who committed the crime, but no solid proof yet.
کارآگاهان نظریه‌ای درباره اینکه چه کسی مرتکب جرم شده بود داشتند، اما هنوز مدرک قطعی نداشتند.
Her theory about the missing files turned out to be completely wrong.
نظریه او درباره پرونده‌های گم‌شده کاملاً غلط از آب درآمد.
miniContext: A theory is a reasoned explanation for how or why something happens, based on observation, evidence, or logical analysis, though it may not yet be proven true. Scientists build a theory to explain natural phenomena, and detectives form a theory about a crime before they have conclusive proof. In everyday speech, a theory can be more of a guess, but in science it specifically means a well-supported explanation.

examples: The farmers utilize rainwater to irrigate their crops during the dry season.
کشاورزان از آب باران برای آبیاری محصولاتشان در فصل خشک استفاده می‌کنند.
Students should utilize the library's resources before writing their research papers.
دانش‌آموزان باید قبل از نوشتن مقالات تحقیقی‌شان از منابع کتابخانه استفاده کنند.
The architect utilized natural light to reduce the building's energy costs.
معمار از نور طبیعی استفاده کرد تا هزینه‌های انرژی ساختمان را کاهش دهد.
miniContext: To utilize something means to make practical use of it, especially a resource, tool, or skill that might otherwise go unused. Companies utilize data to improve their products, and a smart traveler utilizes local knowledge to find better deals. The word is slightly more formal than the simple verb 'use,' often appearing in technical, academic, or business writing.

examples: The climbers began to descend the mountain as the weather turned dangerous.
کوهنوردان شروع کردند از کوه پایین بیایند چون آب‌وهوا خطرناک شده بود.
Passengers were asked to descend the stairs slowly because the elevator was out of service.
از مسافران خواسته شد به‌آرامی از پله‌ها پایین بیایند چون آسانسور خراب بود.
A sudden silence seemed to descend over the room when the principal walked in.
وقتی مدیر وارد شد، سکوتی ناگهانی به نظر می‌رسید بر اتاق نازل شده باشد.
miniContext: To descend means to move downward, whether climbing down a mountain, walking down a staircase, or an airplane descending toward a runway. The word can also be used figuratively, as when darkness descends at dusk or a mood of gloom descends over a gathering. Its opposite, ascend, describes upward movement, and the two words often appear together in descriptions of travel or change in altitude.

examples: The coach decided to eliminate unnecessary drills from the team's practice schedule.
مربی تصمیم گرفت تمرینات غیرضروری را از برنامه تمرین تیم حذف کند.
Doctors ran several tests to eliminate other possible causes of her symptoms.
پزشکان چند آزمایش انجام دادند تا سایر دلایل احتمالی علائم او را حذف کنند.
The new filter helps eliminate most of the dust in the air.
فیلتر جدید به از بین بردن بیشتر گرد و غبار موجود در هوا کمک می‌کند.
miniContext: To eliminate something means to remove or get rid of it completely, often as part of a process of narrowing down options or improving a situation. Doctors eliminate possible diagnoses one by one before reaching a conclusion, and a company might eliminate an entire department to cut costs. The word suggests a deliberate, thorough removal rather than something disappearing on its own.

examples: Blood needs to circulate properly throughout the body to keep organs healthy.
خون باید به‌درستی در سراسر بدن گردش کند تا اندام‌ها سالم بمانند.
Rumors began to circulate around the office about upcoming layoffs.
شایعاتی درباره اخراج‌های آینده در دفتر شروع به پخش شدن کرد.
Fans helped circulate warm air throughout the large hall during the event.
پنکه‌ها به گردش هوای گرم در سراسر سالن بزرگ در طول برنامه کمک کردند.
miniContext: To circulate means to move continuously through a system, or to spread from person to person. Blood circulates through the body carrying oxygen, air circulates through a ventilation system, and news or rumors circulate through a community or office. The word captures the idea of constant movement, whether of a substance, a document, or information passing from one person to the next.
